seoTitle: Response Time Percentiles per Endpoint from Access Logs
metaDescription: Compute p50, p90, p95 and p99 latency per endpoint from logs with request time. Pick the unit and merge numeric IDs. Free.
intro: Groups requests by route and computes latency percentiles with the nearest-rank method.
why:
Averages hide slow requests. Percentiles show how bad the slow ones are. The tool groups by endpoint, optionally merging /items/12 and /items/13 into /items/:id.

The log must record the duration: add $request_time to nginx or %D to Apache. Results were checked against a Python nearest-rank calculation.
howTo: Add the duration to your log format.
Set the unit and whether to merge IDs.
Sort by p95, p99 or count.

faq.a: Nearest rank: the smallest value with at least p percent of values at or below it.

faq.q: What if my log has a different layout?
faq.a: Use the regex option with a named group rt, and optionally path.
$request_time is in seconds with millisecond resolution; Apache %D is microseconds.
No. Everything is processed in your browser and nothing is sent. Logs can hold IP addresses and tokens, so the page does not write them into the address bar.
